questions.question: Which of the following poems is found in the Vercelli Book and contains the 'Dream of the Rood'?
questions.explanation: The Vercelli Book holds Andreas, Elene and The Fates of the Apostles alongside The Dream of the Rood.
questions.explanation_hi: Vercelli Book me 'Dream of the Rood' ke saath-saath 'Andreas', 'Elene' aur 'The Fates of the Apostles' ye sabhi kavitayein shamil hain.

questions.question: The manuscript 'Cotton Vitellius A.xv' is primarily famous for containing which epic?
questions.explanation: Cotton Vitellius A.xv is known above all for holding both Beowulf and Judith.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Cotton Vitellius A.xv' manuscript mukhya roop se 'Beowulf' aur 'Judith' dono kavitayo ko sametne ke liye prasiddh hai.

questions.question: In Beowulf, what is the term used for the 'blood-price' or 'man-price' paid to a family for a killing?
questions.explanation: The fixed payment made to a dead man's family to settle a killing is called wergild, the 'man-price'.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Beowulf' me kisi hatya ke badle parivar ko chukaye jane wale 'blood-price' ya 'man-price' (muavze) ko 'Wergild' kaha jata hai.

questions.question: Which Anglo-Saxon poem is considered the earliest autobiographical poem in English literature, featuring a wandering minstrel?
questions.explanation: Widsith is usually called the earliest autobiographical poem in English, spoken by a wandering minstrel.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Widsith' ko English literature ki sabse purani autobiographical kavita mana jata hai, jisme ek ghumantu charan (wandering minstrel) ka varnan hai.

questions.question: King Alfred translated several Latin works into Old English. Which of these was NOT translated by him or under his direct supervision?
questions.explanation: The Ormulum was not translated by Alfred or under his direction — it belongs to the Middle English period.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Ormulum' ka anuvad King Alfred ya unke nirdeshan me nahi hua tha (yeh Middle English kaal ki rachna hai).

questions.question: Cynewulf is known for signing his name in runic characters in his poems. In how many extant poems does his signature appear?
questions.explanation: Cynewulf's runic signature appears in four surviving poems.
questions.explanation_hi: Kavi Cynewulf ke runic aksharo wale hastakshar (signature) kul 4 uplabdh (extant) kavitayo me milte hain.

questions.question: The 'Ubi Sunt' motif, reflecting on the transience of life, is most prominently found in which poem?
questions.explanation: The 'ubi sunt' motif, on how everything earthly passes away, is strongest in The Wanderer.
questions.explanation_hi: Jeevan ki nashwarta (transience of life) ko darshane wala 'Ubi Sunt' motif sabse pramukh roop se 'The Wanderer' kavita me milta hai.

questions.question: Which Old English poem is a fragment of a larger epic and deals with the legendary Gothic king Theodoric?
questions.explanation: Waldere is a fragment of a longer epic and touches on the legendary Gothic king Theodoric.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Waldere' ek bade mahakavya ka ansh (fragment) hai jo pauranik Gothic raja Theodoric se sambandhit hai.

questions.question: The poem 'The Battle of Brunanburh' is found in which historical record?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Brunanburh is preserved inside the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Battle of Brunanburh' kavita 'The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle' namak aitihasik record me milti hai.

questions.question: Who is the speaker in 'The Dream of the Rood'?
questions.explanation: Both the Cross (the Rood) and the Poet (the Dreamer) speak in the poem.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Dream of the Rood' kavita me The Cross (Rood) aur The Poet (Dreamer) dono hi vakta (speaker) ke roop me aate hain.

questions.question: Aelfric of Eynsham is primarily known for his:
questions.explanation: Ælfric of Eynsham is known above all for his Catholic Homilies.
questions.explanation_hi: Aelfric of Eynsham mukhya roop se apne 'Catholic Homilies' (dharmik updesho) ke liye jane jate hain.

questions.question: The 'Junius Manuscript' is also known by what other name?
questions.explanation: The Junius Manuscript is also called the Cædmon Manuscript.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Junius Manuscript' ko 'The Caedmon Manuscript' ke naam se bhi jana jata hai.

questions.question: Which kenning refers to the 'Sea' in Beowulf?
questions.explanation: Beowulf uses whale-road, swan-road and sail-road, all as kennings for the sea.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Beowulf' me samudra (Sea) ke liye 'Whale-road', 'Swan-road' aur 'Sail-road' in sabhi kennings ka prayog hua hai.

questions.question: In 'The Battle of Maldon', who is the English leader who allows the Vikings to cross the causeway out of 'ofermōd' (pride)?
questions.explanation: Byrhtnoth, the English leader, lets the Vikings cross the causeway out of ofermōd — too much pride.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Battle of Maldon' me English neta Byrhtnoth apne 'ofermōd' (atyadhik abhiman/pride) ke karan Vikings ko rasta par karne ki anumati deta hai.

questions.question: Which of the following works is written in Latin but provides the primary history of the Anglo-Saxon period?
options: Ecclesiastical History of the English People
questions.explanation: The Ecclesiastical History of the English People is written in Latin, yet it is the chief history of the Anglo-Saxon period.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Ecclesiastical History of the English People' Latin bhasha me likhi gayi hai, lekin yeh Anglo-Saxon kaal ka pramukh itihas pradan karti hai.

questions.question: The 'Exeter Book' contains a collection of short, metaphorical poems known as:
questions.explanation: The Exeter Book holds a large collection of short metaphorical poems known as riddles.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Exeter Book' me chhoti aur metaphorical kavitayo ka ek bada sangrah hai jinhe 'Riddles' (paheliya) kaha jata hai.

questions.question: Which poem ends with the line 'That passed away, so may this'?
questions.explanation: The refrain 'That passed away, so may this' comes in Deor.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Deor' kavita me 'That passed away, so may this' pankti (refrain) aati hai.

questions.question: What is the primary meter of Old English poetry?
questions.explanation: The main metre of Old English poetry is alliterative verse.
questions.explanation_hi: Old English poetry ka mukhya meter 'Alliterative Verse' hai.

questions.question: Bede recorded the story of which poet who received the gift of song in a stable?
questions.explanation: Bede records the story of Cædmon, who was given the gift of song in a dream while sleeping among the animals.
questions.explanation_hi: Bede ne kavi Caedmon ki kahani darj ki hai, jinhe ek astabal (stable) me sapne ke dauran geet gane ka vardan mila tha.

questions.question: In Beowulf, who is Grendel a descendant of?
questions.explanation: In Beowulf, Grendel is a descendant of the biblical Cain.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Beowulf' ke anusar rakshas Grendel Biblical patra Cain ka vanshaj (descendant) hai.

questions.question: The 'Sermo Lupi ad Anglos' (Sermon of the Wolf to the English) was written by:
questions.explanation: Sermo Lupi ad Anglos was written by Archbishop Wulfstan.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Sermo Lupi ad Anglos' (Sermon of the Wolf to the English) ki rachna Archbishop Wulfstan ne ki thi.

questions.question: Which poem describes the destruction of a Roman city, likely Bath?
questions.explanation: The Ruin describes the broken remains of an old Roman city, most likely Bath.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Ruin' kavita ek prachin Roman shahar (sambhavtah Bath) ke vinash aur khandaharo ka varnan karti hai.

questions.question: The poem 'Christ and Satan' is found in which manuscript?
questions.explanation: Christ and Satan is found in the Junius Manuscript.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Christ and Satan' kavita 'Junius' manuscript me payi jati hai.

questions.question: Who was the first Christian king of Kent, mentioned in Bede's history?
questions.explanation: Bede's history names Æthelberht as the first Christian king of Kent.
questions.explanation_hi: Bede ke itihas me varnit Kent ke pehle Christian raja Ethelbert the.

questions.question: Which work was intended to be a 'mirror for magistrates', providing moral guidance to rulers?
questions.explanation: Cura Pastoralis (Pastoral Care) was meant to give moral guidance to rulers and churchmen.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Cura Pastoralis' (Pastoral Care) ka uddeshya shasako aur dharmaguruo ko naitik margdarshan dena tha.

questions.question: Which of these characters is the 'loyal thane' who helps Beowulf in his final battle against the dragon?
questions.explanation: Wiglaf is the loyal thane who stands with Beowulf in his last fight against the dragon.
questions.explanation_hi: Dragon ke khilaf aakhiri ladai me Beowulf ki madad karne wala 'loyal thane' (wafadar yoddha) Wiglaf hai.

questions.question: The 'Nowell Codex' was severely damaged in a fire in 1731. Where was it kept?
questions.explanation: The Nowell Codex was badly damaged by fire in 1731, when it was kept at Ashburnham House.
questions.explanation_hi: 1731 me jab 'Nowell Codex' aag me buri tarah kshatigrast hua, tab wah Ashburnham House me rakha gaya tha.

questions.question: The 'Vercelli Book' was discovered in which country?
questions.explanation: The Vercelli Book was found in Italy, in the town of Vercelli.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Vercelli Book' ki khoj Italy (Vercelli shahar) me hui thi.

questions.question: Which poem is an allegorical description of the Resurrection, using a mythical bird?
questions.explanation: The Phoenix tells of the Resurrection through the figure of a mythical bird.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Phoenix' kavita ek pauranik pakshi ke madhyam se Resurrection (punarjeevan) ka roopak (allegorical) varnan karti hai.

questions.question: In the poem 'The Seafarer', the speaker contrasts the hardships of the sea with:
questions.explanation: In The Seafarer the speaker sets the hardship of the sea against the comforts of life in the town.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Seafarer' kavita me vakta samudra ki kathinaiyo ki tulna shahar ke aaramdayak jeevan (comforts of city life) se karta hai.

questions.question: Who was the last Anglo-Saxon king of England?
questions.explanation: Harold Godwinson was the last Anglo-Saxon king of England.
questions.explanation_hi: England ke aakhiri Anglo-Saxon raja Harold Godwinson the.

questions.question: The term 'Scop' refers to:
questions.explanation: In the Anglo-Saxon period a scop was an oral poet who recited verse in the hall.
questions.explanation_hi: Anglo-Saxon kaal me 'Scop' shabd ka prayog ek 'oral poet' (maukhik kavi ya charan) ke liye kiya jata tha.

questions.question: Which manuscript contains the largest collection of Old English riddles?
questions.explanation: The largest collection of Old English riddles is in the Exeter Book.
questions.explanation_hi: Old English riddles (paheliyo) ka sabse bada sangrah 'Exeter Book' manuscript me milta hai.

questions.question: Which dialect was the standard for most surviving Old English literature?
questions.explanation: West Saxon is the dialect in which most surviving Old English literature was written down.
questions.explanation_hi: Adhikansh bache hue Old English sahitya ke liye 'West Saxon' dialect hi manak (standard) bhasha thi.

questions.question: The 'Anglo-Saxon Chronicle' was initiated during the reign of:
questions.explanation: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle was begun in the reign of Alfred the Great.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Anglo-Saxon Chronicle' ki shuruat King Alfred the Great ke shasankaal me hui thi.

questions.question: Which poem features a woman exiled and living in a cave/earth-hall?
questions.explanation: The Wife's Lament speaks for an exiled woman made to live in a cave or earth-hall.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Wife's Lament' kavita me ek nirvasit (exiled) mahila ka varnan hai jo ek gufa ya 'earth-hall' me rehne ko majboor hai.

questions.question: In 'The Fight at Finnsburg', the conflict is between which two groups?
questions.explanation: The fighting in The Fight at Finnsburg is between the Danes and the Frisians.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Fight at Finnsburg' me sangharsh Danes aur Frisians ke beech hota hai.

questions.question: Which work is a translation of a late antique Roman philosopher's dialogue with a lady?
questions.explanation: Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy is a dialogue between a late Roman philosopher and Lady Philosophy, turned into Old English.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy' ek Roman darshanik aur Lady Philosophy ke beech ke samvad ka Old English anuvad hai.

questions.question: The poem 'Judith' is based on a story from:
questions.explanation: The poem Judith is based on a story from the Apocrypha of the Old Testament.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Judith' kavita Old Testament ke 'The Apocrypha' ki ek kahani par aadharit hai.

questions.question: What is the function of the 'Caesura' in Old English verse?
options: A pause in the middle of a line
questions.explanation: In Old English verse the caesura is the pause in the middle of a line.
questions.explanation_hi: Old English verse me 'Caesura' ka kaam ek pankti ke beech me thehrav (pause in the middle of a line) dena hai.

questions.question: The poem 'The Fates of the Apostles' is signed by which poet?
questions.explanation: The Fates of the Apostles carries Cynewulf's runic signature.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Fates of the Apostles' kavita me kavi Cynewulf ke runic hastakshar milte hain.

questions.question: In Beowulf, who is the King of the Danes?
questions.explanation: Hrothgar is the king of the Danes in Beowulf.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Beowulf' kavita me Hrothgar Danes ka raja (King of the Danes) hai.

questions.question: The 'Gnomes' found in Anglo-Saxon manuscripts are essentially:
questions.explanation: The 'gnomes' in Anglo-Saxon manuscripts are maxims or proverbs.
questions.explanation_hi: Anglo-Saxon manuscripts me milne wale 'Gnomes' mool roop se 'Maxims or proverbs' (kahawatein ya suktiya) hote hain.

questions.question: Which poem is considered one of the earliest examples of a 'Revenge Tragedy' structure in embryonic form?
questions.explanation: The Fight at Finnsburg is often read as an early, undeveloped form of the revenge-tragedy pattern.
questions.explanation_hi: 'The Fight at Finnsburg' ko shuruati roop (embryonic form) me 'Revenge Tragedy' structure ke sabse purane udaharan me se ek mana jata hai.

questions.question: Athelstan's victory over the combined forces of the Scots, Irish, and Vikings is celebrated in:
questions.explanation: Æthelstan's victory over the combined Scots, Irish and Viking forces is celebrated in The Battle of Brunanburh.
questions.explanation_hi: Scots, Irish aur Vikings ki sanyukt sena par Raja Athelstan ki jeet ka jashn 'The Battle of Brunanburh' kavita me manaya gaya hai.

questions.question: Which poem tells the story of the fall of man but is thought to be a translation from an Old Saxon original?
questions.explanation: Genesis B tells the fall of man and is taken to be a translation from an Old Saxon original.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Genesis B' manushya ke patan (fall of man) ki kahani batati hai aur ise mool Old Saxon kavita ka anuvad mana jata hai.

questions.question: The 'Cotton Vitellius A.xv' was named after:
options: A Roman Emperor's bust on the shelf
questions.explanation: Cotton Vitellius A.xv is named after the bust of the Roman emperor Vitellius that stood on the shelf in Sir Robert Cotton's library.
questions.explanation_hi: 'Cotton Vitellius A.xv' ka naam Sir Robert Cotton ki library ke us book-shelf ke upar rakhi Roman samrat Vitellius ki moorti (bust) ke naam par pada tha.

questions.question: Which epic features the monster Grendel's mother as an antagonist?
questions.explanation: Grendel's mother appears as an antagonist in the epic Beowulf.
questions.explanation_hi: Grendel ki maa (Grendel's mother) mahakavya 'Beowulf' me ek antagonist (khalnayika) ke roop me aati hai.

questions.question: What literary device is used in the phrase 'He was not slow to act' in Old English poetry?
questions.explanation: Saying far less than is meant, as in 'He was not slow to act', is litotes.
questions.explanation_hi: 'He was not slow to act' jaise nakaratmak shabdo se sakaratmak arth dene wale understatement ko 'Litotes' kehte hain.

questions.question: Who was the 'Scholar-King' who promoted the use of English over Latin for education?
questions.explanation: Alfred is called the Scholar-King; he pushed for English rather than Latin in teaching.
questions.explanation_hi: King Alfred ko 'Scholar-King' kaha jata hai, jinhone shiksha ke liye Latin ki jagah English bhasha ke prayog ko badhava diya.

quote.text: Where has the horse gone? Where the rider? Where the giver of treasure?
